sections.h2: Where do I go for property tax questions in Hoke County, NC?
sections.html:
The Hoke County Tax Office has two departments, and both are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The Assessor lists, appraises and assesses all taxable property, and Collections bills and collects tax on real estate, personal property and delinquent motor vehicles.

The post office box is 1557 in Raeford, ZIP 28376, and the phone line is 910-875-8751. The appraisal office keeps weekday office hours. According to the county, the roll covers about 28,000 parcels of land, 700 businesses and 40,000 motor vehicles, which is a lot of ground for a county of about 390 square miles of land.

Hoke County was founded in 1911, and Raeford, incorporated in 1901, became the county seat. The county sits between Fayetteville and Cumberland County to the east and Pinehurst and Moore County to the west, and part of Fort Bragg lies on county land.

sections.h2: What rates and fees appear on a Hoke County tax bill?
sections.html:
A bill is built from the county rate, any city rate, a fire district rate and a solid waste fee. The county's tax rates page explains that rates apply to each $100 of value, and that city properties do not get the fire district tax or the solid waste fee.

Rates and fees as printed in the Hoke County tax rates and fees worked examples
Line on the billFigure printed by the county
Hoke County rate.73 per $100 of value
City of Raeford rate.48 per $100 of value
North Raeford fire district rate.10 per $100 of value
Solid waste fee$130.00 per unit in the sample bill

Fire district rates differ by district, so request from the Tax Office the sheet that lists the district for your parcel, and confirm the current Raeford rate if the house is inside city limits.

sections.h2: When did Hoke County last revalue property, and what is next?
sections.html:
The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2022. Notices went to all Hoke County taxpayers on February 3, 2022, and the next revaluation is set for January 1, 2030, with work starting two years before.

The county cites G.S. 105-286, which requires reappraisal at least every eight years. Between cycles your assessed value on real property stays tied to the January 1, 2022 market level unless you add improvements or the parcel changes. Ask the assessor how a sale price compares with the 2022 value on your parcel.

In the county's words, an appraisal sets each owner's share of the taxes that support schools, roads, parks, public health, libraries, police and fire protection. The amount you pay depends on your property value and the rates adopted each year by elected county and city or town officials.

sections.h2: What is the route for contesting a Hoke County assessment?
sections.html:
The Notice of Appeal of Assessment goes to the Tax Assessor ahead of the equalization board's adjournment. The county advertises that date in the local paper and online, and the assessor's office can confirm it.

  • One form per parcel, signed by the owner or a representative (an attorney, or an attorney in fact holding a power of attorney when the owner is not a corporation).
  • Evidence can be an appraisal, sales of similar properties, income and expense statements or replacement cost, and copies go in with the form.
  • The owner must show the value substantially exceeds true market value on the January 1, 2022 valuation date.
  • The board sets a hearing date and tells you; you can attend or send counsel.

The county's procedures mention informal appeals, and an appraisal already submitted informally need not be sent in again. The next stop after the county board is the Property Tax Commission, with a written notice due 30 days after the mailing of the decision. Statute: G.S. 105-290.

sections.h2: What is the Hoke County payment timeline?
sections.html:
September 1 is the due date. Under G.S. 105-360, paying before January 6 costs face value; from then until February 1 a charge of 2 percent applies, followed by three quarters of a percent per month.

The county lets residents pay online, and the Collections office answers billing questions. The USPS postmark date counts for mail, so keep the envelope. State law lets a county adopt prepayment discounts; ask whether Hoke has one.

Under G.S. 105-355, unpaid tax attaches to the parcel as a lien from the listing date, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure filed where the land lies. A sale is a public auction at the courthouse door, and a person who redeems before confirmation pays the tax plus penalties, interest and costs. See G.S. 105-374.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can Hoke County owners use?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers an elderly or disabled exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferral, and an owner may take only one. The county assessor takes the Form AV-9 filing. Veterans are a large group here, with 6,926 counted by the Census Bureau.

The 2026 thresholds printed by the revenue department are $38,800 for the base income limit and $58,200 for the circuit breaker's upper tier. The state accepts filings through June 1 before the tax year. A transfer of the property triggers the deferred tax under the circuit breaker, so mention it to your attorney before you list. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

sections.h2: How is the Hoke County housing market shaped?
sections.html:
Hoke has grown from 52,082 people at the 2020 count to an estimate of 56,939 in July 2025. The county counts 22,440 housing units and issued 558 building permits during 2025.

Owners occupy 73.0 percent of homes. The midpoint owned home is valued at $219,300, with owner costs of $1,472 monthly where a mortgage exists. Rent runs $1,089, household income is $64,912, and the average trip to work takes 28.8 minutes. Children under 18 are 26.7 percent of residents and seniors 13.1 percent.

The county's economic development page ties the growth to the neighboring military post and describes a past built on cotton, then poultry. Butterball is credited with 600 jobs, and the North Carolina Fall Festival is described as drawing more than 30,000 visitors. Industrial sites with dual rail service connect to two national railroads through the Aberdeen and Rockfish line, the same line whose extension led to the incorporation of Raeford in 1901. Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How should a Hoke County seller handle the tax bill?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from Collections that covers this year and earlier years. Because the lien dates from the listing date, an unpaid current-year bill must be cleared at closing.

  • Have the closing attorney pay taxes from proceeds.
  • Look for a fire district tax and a solid waste fee on the bill if the house sits outside Raeford.
  • Confirm any exclusion filing is current before the sale.
  • Keep your 2022 value notice handy for buyers who ask.

faqs.q: Where is the Hoke County Tax Office?
faqs.a: Both the Assessor and Collections are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. The post office box is 1557 in Raeford, ZIP 28376, and the phone line is 910-875-8751.

faqs.q: When is the next Hoke County revaluation?
faqs.a: It is scheduled for January 1, 2030. The last one took effect January 1, 2022, with notices mailed February 3, 2022, and work begins two years before the effective date.

faqs.q: What is the Hoke County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's tax rates page prints a county rate of .73 per $100 in its examples, a Raeford rate of .48 and a North Raeford fire district rate of .10. A solid waste fee can apply outside city limits, so request the current rate sheet.

faqs.q: What do I file to contest a Hoke County value?
faqs.a: File a Notice of Appeal of Assessment for each parcel with the Tax Assessor before the equalization board adjourns, with evidence such as appraisals or comparable sales. The adjournment date is advertised in the newspaper and on the county website.

faqs.q: Does Hoke County have a fire district tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The county tax rates page lists a fire district rate that is charged on top of the county rate, based on the district where the property sits. City properties do not receive it.
